title: 2024 budget service expansions and budget amendment deadlines
subtitle: Climate-aligned growth, transit expansion, home energy retrofits, reserves and police budget process were also discussed.
overview: The Strategic Planning and Budget Committee held its second 2024 budget meeting, focused on the Climate Aligned Growth priority. Staff presented the preliminary budget, and the committee recommended a series of service expansions for inclusion in the 2024 operating budget. These cover a water and wastewater health and safety specialist, asset management staff, roads vegetation and traffic signal staff, more bus and ION service hours, a Conestoga College UPass, and a home energy retrofit pilot.

The committee also recommended a notice deadline of November 29, 2023 for motions to amend the final budget, ahead of final budget day on December 13. A motion asking police leadership to present a draft budget to Regional Council before it is finalized was defeated on a tie {{vote:m7}}.

For residents, these recommendations shape the 2024 tax levy and the services they receive. Staff reported a 7.3% tax impact with the proposed expansions included, before police figures. Council will make the final decisions later.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended including a Health and Safety Specialist for water and wastewater in the 2024 operating budget {{vote:m1}}.
The committee recommended adding an Asset Performance Analyst and an Asset Management Planner to the 2024 operating budget {{vote:m2}}.
The committee recommended expansions for horticultural services, urban forestry, active transportation and traffic signal technicians {{vote:m3}}.
The committee recommended Conestoga College UPass service, subject to a successful student referendum, plus added GRT bus and ION service hours {{vote:m4}}.
The committee recommended including the Home Energy Retrofit Program service expansion in the 2024 operating budget {{vote:m5}}.
The committee recommended that motions to amend the final budget be submitted in writing by November 29, 2023, with limited exceptions requiring a two-thirds vote to waive notice {{vote:m6}}.
A motion expressing disappointment at the lack of a response to the February resolution and asking police leadership to present a draft budget before finalizing it was defeated {{vote:m7}}.

debate: On timing, one councillor argued the committee lacked police budget figures needed to decide. Staff said all information on directly delivered services was provided and police numbers would be added, with a police presentation scheduled for November 22. Another councillor said delaying the December approval would push back area municipal tax bills.

On reserves, councillors questioned the planned use of the tax stabilization reserve. Staff and the CAO said reserves act as shock absorbers because the Region cannot borrow for operations or run a deficit, and recommended keeping the working funds target at its current level. Staff cited the credit rating agency's warning about rising debt and falling reserves.

On transit, councillors raised concerns about fare revenue assumptions, evening LRT frequency after 8 p.m. for students and retail workers, and Mobility Plus unaccommodated trips. Staff said bus route 7 would supplement evening service, and promised more detail on November 1.

Councillors asked about accessibility of pedestrian crosswalk buttons, hazardous tree removals and whether paving boulevards would be cheaper. Staff said they would look at accessibility and that vegetation reduces flooding and heat.
In support of the police motion, its mover said Council sets how police estimates are presented and that the Board had not responded to the February resolution. The motion was defeated on a tie.
